title: Extension of Continuing Appropriations Act, 2022
official_summary:
Extension of Continuing Appropriations Act, 2022

This joint resolution provides continuing FY2022 appropriations to federal agencies through March 15, 2022. It is known as a continuing resolution (CR) and prevents a government shutdown that would otherwise occur if the FY2022 appropriations bills have not been enacted when the existing CR expires on March 11, 2022.

The joint resolution also (1) extends the temporary scheduling order issued by the Drug Enforcement Administration to place fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, and (2) increases the limit on the value of the defense articles and services that the President is authorized to draw down to address unforeseen emergencies.

summary.headline: A short-term spending bill that keeps federal agencies funded through March 15, 2022, and makes two related changes on fentanyl scheduling and emergency weapons transfers.
summary.what_it_does: This joint resolution is a continuing resolution that keeps federal agencies funded past the March 11, 2022 deadline, so the government does not shut down while full FY2022 spending bills are still pending. It extends through March 15, 2022. It also extends a temporary Drug Enforcement Administration order that places fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act. Finally, it raises the dollar limit on defense equipment and services the President can release quickly in unforeseen emergencies.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agency employees and federal workers
who_it_affects.how: Their agencies receive continued funding, which keeps the government open and avoids a shutdown during the extension period.

who_it_affects.group: People who rely on federal government services
who_it_affects.how: Services funded by federal agencies continue without interruption through March 15, 2022.
The temporary federal scheduling order for these substances remains in effect, so related handling and possession rules continue to apply.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign governments receiving U.S. defense equipment
who_it_affects.how: The President can provide a larger value of defense articles and services in an emergency without waiting for new authorization.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted March 11, 2022, and funding runs through March 15, 2022.
